texts: good. the condition routes to a fireable rule: the Keeper, the lantern, the untended state the leaving results in, the overnight timing and "before dawn" on the dying are all carried, and each leaving occurrence gets its own death event.

mixed: the rule fires and the rest is right - "untended" as a state of the lantern, "goes out" kept whole as one verb, "before dawn" as an upper time bound - but "through the night" survives only as a plain night time-stamp, so the condition widens to a lantern untended at any point in the night rather than one untended for the whole night. Rewrite as: "When a lantern is untended from dusk until dawn, the lantern goes out before dawn." - a from/until pair is the form that records a span.

mixed: the atoms are right, but "A Keeper" with an ordinary verb is read as one particular unnamed Keeper, so the sentence records that one keeper's habit instead of the standing practice of Keepers; a singular indefinite never becomes a general rule here. Rewrite as: "Keepers refresh the mire-essence and trim the wick during the night." - the bare plural is what turns it into a rule reaching every Keeper.
